key_insight: A graph self-attention neural network can classify weld defects accurately from very few labeled images by exploiting patch-based graph features instead of relying on large training sets.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical low-data inspection method for welding quality control, reducing annotation cost while preserving strong defect-detection performance in industrial settings.
method: Builds a graph neural network for weld image classification.
Uses patch-based node construction to reduce computation.
Adds self-attention to strengthen node feature representation.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on Al5083 and SS304 using only 5% of training data, the model achieved 82.0% and 94.8% accuracy, outperforming ResNet18 by 5.2% and 2.4% respectively.
watch_item: Performance is shown on public datasets with limited training splits, so real plant deployment may still require validation under domain shift, noise, and class imbalance.
paper_title: Few-Shot Welding Defect Detection via Graph Self-Attention Neural Network
